title: Kasivisvesvara Temple & Stepwells, Lakkundi
summary: Masterwork of Kalyana Chalukyan soapstone carving featuring pierced stone doorframes, twin shrines, and nearby geometric stepped wells.
description: Once an imperial mint and cultural center (Lokkigundi) under the Kalyana Chalukyas, Lakkundi preserves scores of 11th-century temples and stepped wells (kalyanis). Its Kasivisvesvara Temple is celebrated for deeply undercut stone toranas, twin facing sanctuaries, and delicate filigree carving.
verifiedFacts: Patronized during the 10th–12th centuries CE, notably under Jain philanthropist Attimabbe and Chalukyan kings.
Preserves intricate stepwells including Muskin Bhavi and Channabasavanna Bhavi.
ASI maintains an on-site sculpture museum displaying over 100 recovered Chalukyan artifacts.
preservationNote: Managed as a protected archaeological village cluster by the Archaeological Survey of India.
altText: Ornate 11th-century Kalyana Chalukya soapstone facade of Kasivisvesvara Temple at Lakkundi in Gadag.

title: Lakkundi Utsava
summary: Celebration of Kalyana Chalukyan architecture, Hindustani music, and Gadag's folk traditions set amidst Lakkundi's illuminated temples.
description: Organized by the Gadag district administration and Kannada and Culture Department, Lakkundi Utsava brings classical musicians—including alumni of Pandit Puttaraj Gawai's Veereshwara Punyashrama—together with regional folk troupes beside Lakkundi's 11th-century monuments.
verifiedFacts: Celebrates Lakkundi's legacy as a cradle of Kalyana Chalukyan architecture and Attimabbe's literary patronage.
Features folk art processions, Hindustani concerts, and heritage walks to ancient stepwells.
Promotes heritage conservation awareness across Gadag district.
preservationNote: Cultural programming highlights clean preservation of Lakkundi's 101 historic stepwells.
altText: Lakkundi Utsava Cultural Festival in Gadag

title: Hoysaleswara Temple, Halebidu
recognitionOrEra: UNESCO World Heritage Site Ref. 1670 · 12th Century CE
summary: Twin-sanctum Hoysala royal monument at ancient Dorasamudra adorned with continuous soapstone friezes of elephants, cavalry, and Hindu epics.
description: Constructed in the 12th century CE in the Hoysala capital of Dorasamudra (modern Halebidu), Hoysaleswara Temple is an extraordinary twin-shrine chloritic schist monument dedicated to Shiva. Its outer wall wraps around two star-shaped sanctums in unbroken horizontal bands of sculpted elephants, makaras, swans, and epic scenes.
verifiedFacts: Inscribed by UNESCO on September 18, 2023 as part of 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas' (Ref. 1670).
Begun around 1121 CE during King Vishnuvardhana's reign and completed by master architect Ketamalla.
Features two monumental monolithic Nandi pavilions facing the twin east entrances.
preservationNote: Conserved by ASI alongside an archaeological sculpture museum on the Dwarasamudra tank embankment.
altText: Twin-shrine soapstone exterior of Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu in Hassan district.

title: Gommateshwara Monolith, Shravanabelagola
summary: 17.5-meter freestanding granite statue of Jain Tirthankara-prince Bahubali atop Vindhyagiri Hill, commissioned by Ganga minister Chavundaraya.
description: Carved from a single fine-grained granite block atop Vindhyagiri (Indragiri) Hill around 981 CE by sculptor Arishtanemi under Western Ganga commander Chavundaraya, the Gommateshwara Bahubali statue is one of the tallest freestanding stone monoliths of the ancient world, flanked by Chandragiri Hill's early Jain basadis.
verifiedFacts: Stands 57 feet (about 17.5 meters) tall atop Vindhyagiri Hill, approached via over 600 rock-cut steps.
Base bears trilingual inscriptions in Kannada, Tamil, and Marathi praising patron Chavundaraya.
Adjacent Chandragiri Hill preserves Mauryan-era inscriptions linking Chandragupta Maurya and Bhadrabahu.
preservationNote: Protected by ASI with strictly scheduled scaffolding protocols during the twelve-year anointment.
altText: Monumental 981 CE granite statue of Gommateshwara Bahubali at Shravanabelagola in Hassan district.

title: Mahamastakabhisheka of Shravanabelagola
summary: Grand twelve-year ceremonial anointment of the 17.5-meter Gommateshwara statue with water, milk, sugarcane juice, saffron, and sandalwood paste.
description: Held once every twelve years atop Vindhyagiri Hill in Shravanabelagola, the Mahamastakabhisheka draws Jain ascetics and devotees worldwide to perform sacred head-anointment (abhisheka) of the 981 CE Bahubali monolith from a specially engineered steel scaffold.
verifiedFacts: Documented historically for over a millennium, with the most recent observance held in February 2018.
Ritual liquids include purified water, tender coconut water, sugarcane juice, milk, saffron, and turmeric.
Accompanied by scholarly conferences on Prakrit, Sanskrit, and early Kannada Jain literature.
preservationNote: ASI oversees non-abrasive rinsing and granite conservation immediately after every ceremony.
altText: Sacred Mahamastakabhisheka ceremonial anointment at the Gommateshwara monolith in Shravanabelagola.

title: Galageshwara Temple, Galaganatha
summary: Stepped pyramidal sandstone shrine rising cleanly beside the confluence of the Varada and Tungabhadra rivers.
description: Standing along the scenic confluence of the Tungabhadra and Varada rivers in Haveri taluk, the 11th-century Galageshwara Temple features a striking tiered pyramidal shikhara and an expansive hall supported by lathe-turned Chalukyan stone columns.
verifiedFacts: Constructed in the 11th century CE under Kalyana Chalukyan patronage.
Positioned at the confluence (sangama) of the Varada and Tungabhadra rivers.
Protected as a Monument of National Importance by the Archaeological Survey of India.
preservationNote: Riverbank stone retaining walls protect the foundation against seasonal Tungabhadra monsoon swells.
altText: Pyramidal stone shikhara and mandapa of Galageshwara Temple at Galaganatha in Haveri district.

title: Kaginele Haridasa Bhakti & Shishunala Tatvapada Heritage
summary: Devotional Kannada keertana heritage of 16th-century poet-saint Kanakadasa at Kaginele alongside Shishunala Sharif's mystic tatvapada songs.
description: Haveri district holds a revered place in Kannada devotional music through Kaginele, center of 16th-century Haridasa poet-reformer Kanakadasa ('Kagineleyadi Keshava'), and Shishunala, home to 19th-century mystic Sant Shishunala Sharif whose colloquial tatvapada lyrics bridge Hindu and Sufi philosophies.
verifiedFacts: Kanakadasa authored classics including Mohanatarangini, Nalacharitre, Ramadhanya Charitre, and hundreds of keertanas.
Sant Shishunala Sharif (1819–1889 CE) studied under Guru Govinda Bhatta in Kalasa-Shishunala.
Kaginele Development Authority maintains temples, lakes, and cultural halls commemorating Kanakadasa.
preservationNote: Performed continuously by Sugama Sangeetha vocalists, folk singers, and classical Carnatic musicians across Karnataka.
altText: Kaginele Haridasa and Shishunala Sharif Musical Heritage in Haveri

sources.title: Haveri District Cultural Heritage — Kaginele & Shishunala

title: Kalaburagi Fort & Jama Masjid
summary: First capital citadel of the Bahmani Sultanate enclosing 15 defensive bastions and the unique 63-dome completely covered Jama Masjid of 1367 CE.
description: Fortified by Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah after establishing the Bahmani Sultanate in 1347 CE, Kalaburagi Fort encloses a remarkable 1367 CE Jama Masjid designed by Rafi of Qazvin—unique in India for having no open courtyard, instead sheltering worshippers beneath a forest of stilted arches and 63 small domes.
verifiedFacts: Jama Masjid (completed 1367 CE under Muhammad Shah I) spans roughly 38,000 sq ft under arched vaults and 63 domes.
Fort ramparts retain the 29-foot historic Bara Gazi Tope iron cannon atop a watchtower.
Protected as a Monument of National Importance by the Archaeological Survey of India.
preservationNote: ASI maintains the vaulted mosque arches, moat walls, and the historic Bala Hisar citadel.
altText: Vaulted arches and multi-domed roofline of the historic Jama Masjid inside Kalaburagi Fort.

sources.title: Kalaburagi Fort & Jama Masjid ASI Record

title: Sannati & Kanaganahalli Buddhist Mahastupa
recognitionOrEra: 3rd Century BCE – 3rd Century CE Mauryan & Satavahana · ASI
summary: Major Bhima river archaeological complex yielding Ashokan edicts and India's only known inscribed stone portrait relief of Emperor Ashoka.
description: Excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India along the Bhima River in Chittapur taluk, Sannati and nearby Kanaganahalli uncovered a monumental Satavahana Mahastupa adorned with sculpted limestone ayaka slabs—including a landmark relief inscribed in Brahmi reading 'Raya Asoko' (King Ashoka).
verifiedFacts: Preserves the only surviving inscribed portrait slab explicitly identifying 'Raya Asoko' in Brahmi script.
Chandralamba Temple courtyard at Sannati yielded Ashokan Major Rock Edicts XII and XIV.
Chronicles continuous habitation from Mauryan (3rd century BCE) through Satavahana (1st–3rd century CE) eras.
preservationNote: Excavated limestone sculptures are conserved by ASI at Sannati and Kalaburagi Archaeological Museum.
altText: Excavated limestone stupa remains at the Sannati–Kanaganahalli archaeological site in Kalaburagi district.

title: Madikeri Fort & Raja's Seat
recognitionOrEra: 17th–19th Century Haleri & Mysore Eras · State Protected
summary: Hilltop citadel originally founded by Muddu Raja in the 17th century and rebuilt in granite, beside the scenic Raja's Seat pavilion.
description: Commanding Madikeri town, Madikeri Fort dates to Muddu Raja's late 17th-century mud citadel before being rebuilt in stone under Tipu Sultan and expanded with a two-storey palace by Lingarajendra Wadiyar II in 1812–1814 CE. Nearby Raja's Seat served as a sunset pavilion overlooking Kodagu's valley ridges.
verifiedFacts: Encloses a 19th-century heritage palace complex, life-size stone elephants, and the Madikeri Fort Museum.
Adjacent Raja's Seat brick-and-mortar arched pavilion overlooks mist-covered Western Ghats valleys.
Protected under Karnataka State Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage.
preservationNote: Preserved as a public heritage monument housing Kodagu historical artifacts and inscriptions.
altText: Historic building inside Madikeri Fort in Kodagu district, Karnataka.

sources.title: Madikeri Fort & Raja's Seat Heritage Profile

title: Talakaveri & Tula Sankramana
summary: Sacred annual autumn gathering at Brahmagiri Hill marking the traditional swelling of the Kaveri headwater spring (Tirthodbhava).
description: Every mid-October on Tula Sankramana, thousands of pilgrims ascend Brahmagiri Hill at Talakaveri—source of the Kaveri River—alongside nearby Bhagamandala Triveni Sangama to witness the sacred 'Tirthodbhava' spring surge inside the Brahma Kundike.
verifiedFacts: Located on the slopes of Brahmagiri Hill at about 1,276 meters above sea level in Kodagu.
Observed annually on Tula Sankramana according to the traditional solar calendar.
Closely linked with Kodava and Karnataka riverine reverence for River Kaveri.
preservationNote: Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary rules protect headwater slopes from deforestation and waste.
altText: Talakaveri Temple complex and sacred tank at the headwaters of the Kaveri River in Kodagu.

title: Kodava Puttari Harvest & Akki Otti Heritage
summary: Post-monsoon rice harvest celebration centered around fresh paddy sheaves, steamed kadambuttu rice balls, akki otti flatbreads, and bamboo shoot curries.
description: Puttari ('New Rice') is Kodagu's signature harvest festival held on the full moon of November–December. Families gather at ancestral Ainmane homes to ceremonially cut fresh rice stalks, prepare spiced sweet tambuttu, steamed kadambuttu, crisp akki otti, and seasonal bamboo shoot (baimbale) curries.
verifiedFacts: Celebrated around the Rohini nakshatra full moon following the monsoon paddy harvest.
Features traditional Kodava dishes including Akki Otti, Kadambuttu, Noolputtu, and Pandi Curry.
Accompanied by folk dances such as Kolat (stick dance) and Bolakaat.
preservationNote: Ainmane okka gatherings sustain traditional recipes and native Kodagu paddy varieties.
altText: Forested hills of Kodagu overlooking the valleys near Madikeri, heartland of Puttari harvest traditions.

title: Kolaramma & Someshwara Temples, Kolar
summary: Chola-period granite Kolaramma temple rich in Tamil-Kannada inscriptions alongside the ornate Vijayanagara Someshwara kalyana mandapa.
description: Representing ancient Kuvalalapura under the Western Gangas and Cholas, Kolar's historic center preserves two landmark monuments: the 11th-century L-shaped Kolaramma Temple—inscribed with royal Chola records—and the sprawling Someshwara Temple famed for its intricately sculpted Vijayanagara marriage hall.
verifiedFacts: Kolaramma Temple dates in its surviving granite form to Rajendra Chola I in the early 11th century CE.
Someshwara Temple preserves a celebrated Vijayanagara-period kalyana mandapa and monolithic pillared corridors.
Both complexes are protected Monuments of National Importance under the ASI.
preservationNote: ASI protects the granite epigraphic panels and stepped kalyani tank at Someshwara.
altText: Granite Dravidian vimana and enclosure walls of the Kolaramma Temple complex in Kolar.

title: Avani Ramalingeshwara Heritage & Shivaratri Fair
summary: Nolamba-Ganga granite temple cluster at Avani hosting an annual Maha Shivaratri car festival and traditional cattle fair.
description: Surrounded by granite boulders in Mulbagal taluk, Avani hosts a 10th-century Nolamba-period temple group (Lakshmanalingeshwara, Bharateshwara, Shatrugnalingeshwara, and Ramalingeshwara) alongside vibrant Maha Shivaratri processions and rural fairs.
verifiedFacts: Temples at Avani date back to the 10th century CE under Nolamba Pallava and Ganga patronage.
Annual Maha Shivaratri Jatra combines temple chariot processions with a historic regional cattle market.
Protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.
preservationNote: ASI preserves the sculpted Nolamba stone reliefs on the temple exterior.
altText: Avani Ramalingeshwara Temple Complex and Fair in Kolar

title: Mahadeva Temple, Itagi
summary: Crowning Kalyana Chalukyan sanctuary consecrated in 1112 CE and praised in its stone inscription as 'Devalaya Chakravarti' (Emperor of Temples).
description: Built in 1112 CE by Mahadeva, general of Chalukya Emperor Vikramaditya VI, the Mahadeva Temple at Itagi in Koppal district showcases deeply carved makara toranas, miniature tower niches, and a grand 68-pillar open sabhamantapa set beside a stepped water tank.
verifiedFacts: Dated firmly to 1112 CE by an inscription erected under Vikramaditya VI's commander Mahadeva.
Referred to in contemporary Kannada epigraphs as 'Devalaya Chakravarti' (Emperor among Temples).
Protected as a Monument of National Importance by the Archaeological Survey of India.
preservationNote: ASI maintains the soapstone carvings and surrounding temple tank enclosure in Kuknur taluk.
altText: Carved Kalyana Chalukya superstructure of the 1112 CE Mahadeva Temple at Itagi in Koppal district.

sources.title: Mahadeva Temple at Itagi Monument Record

title: Kinhal (Kinnal) Painted Wood Craft
summary: Lightweight carved wooden figurines, temple panels, and birds coated in tamarind-seed paste, pebble-chalk gesso, and luminous natural colors.
description: Practiced by Chitragara artisan families in Kinhal village of Koppal district—whose ancestors were associated with the Vijayanagara court murals at nearby Hampi and Anegundi—Kinhal Craft transforms lightweight polki wood with tamarind-seed paste ('kitta'), cloth, chalk gesso, and bright hand-painted lacquer finishes.
verifiedFacts: Awarded Geographical Indication Application No. 212 in 2011.
Artisans use locally grown lightweight timber joined with tamarind-seed paste and cotton-jute paste.
Historical Chitragara guilds contributed woodwork and murals at Hampi's Pampapati temple.
preservationNote: Master-artisan workshops in Kinhal train younger Chitragara craftspeople under GI cooperative initiatives.
altText: Hand-painted wooden figurines and toys crafted by Kinhal artisans in Koppal district.

sources.title: Geographical Indications Registry — Application No. 212 (Kinhal Toys)

title: Daria Daulat Bagh & Srirangapatna Fort
recognitionOrEra: 1784 CE Teakwood Palace & River Island Fort · ASI
summary: Garden pavilion wrapped in vivid 18th-century murals inside the historic Kaveri river island fortress of Srirangapatna.
description: Set in manicured gardens on Srirangapatna river island, Daria Daulat Bagh was built in 1784 CE by Tipu Sultan primarily of teakwood on a raised platform. Its plastered walls and gilded ceilings preserve intricate murals depicting Mysore court processions, allied rulers, and the 1780 Battle of Pollilur.
verifiedFacts: Completed in 1784 CE and conserved as a national museum and monument by the ASI.
Adjacent Srirangapatna Fort encloses the 9th–12th century Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple and Gumbaz.
Murals offer valuable 18th-century visual documentation of South Indian dress, cavalry, and architecture.
preservationNote: Strict light and humidity controls protect the delicate mineral-pigment wall murals inside the palace.
altText: Teakwood colonnaded exterior of Daria Daulat Bagh amidst gardens in Srirangapatna, Mandya district.

title: Melukote Cheluvanarayana Swamy & Vairamudi Festival
summary: Ancient hilltop temple town shaped by Acharya Ramanuja, famed for the midnight Vairamudi diamond-crown procession and Sanskrit Academy.
description: Perched on Yadugiri rocky hills in Mandya district, Melukote (Thirunarayanapuram) became a revered center of Sri Vaishnava scholarship when philosopher Ramanujacharya lived here in the early 12th century CE. Each spring, the temple hosts the Vairamudi Brahmotsava, alongside handloom weaving and the Academy of Sanskrit Research.
verifiedFacts: Chariot and stepped-tank complex preserves ancient inscriptions from Hoysala King Vishnuvardhana and Wadiyar rulers.
Vairamudi crown procession takes place overnight under strict ceremonial traditions.
Melukote is equally celebrated for traditional handloom dhotis and Melukote Puliyogare.
preservationNote: The Academy of Sanskrit Research in Melukote preserves thousands of palm-leaf and paper manuscripts.
altText: Gateway and stone mandapa of Sri Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple at Melukote in Mandya district.

title: Keshava Temple, Somnathapura
recognitionOrEra: UNESCO World Heritage Site Ref. 1670 · 1268 CE
summary: Symmetric trikuta (triple-shrine) Hoysala soapstone temple built in 1268 CE along the Kaveri basin, preserving three intact stellate towers.
description: Commissioned in 1268 CE by Hoysala general Somanatha Dandanayaka under King Narasimha III, the Chennakesava (Keshava) Temple at Somnathapura stands inside a serene cloistered courtyard. Its three star-shaped vimana towers remain intact, showcasing some of master sculptor Mallitamma's finest signed soapstone reliefs.
verifiedFacts: Inscribed by UNESCO on September 18, 2023 as part of 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas' (Ref. 1670).
Features a symmetric trikuta plan with three 16-pointed stellate shrines and 64 miniature perimeter cells.
Over 40 outer wall sculptures bear the signature of master artisan Mallitamma.
preservationNote: Conserved by the Archaeological Survey of India Bengaluru Circle.
altText: Symmetric triple-tower soapstone facade of Chennakesava Temple at Somanathapura in Mysuru district.

title: Bylakuppe Tibetan Heritage & Losar Traditions
summary: One of India's earliest Tibetan settlements hosting Namdroling Monastery, monastic thangka painting, debate traditions, and Losar New Year dances.
description: Established in 1961 on land granted by the Government of Mysore in Periyapatna taluk, Bylakuppe preserves Tibetan Buddhist scholarship, woodblock printing, thangka painting, and vibrant monastic Cham dances during Losar (Tibetan New Year), woven peacefully into Mysuru district's cultural mosaic.
verifiedFacts: Lugsum Samdupling (1961) was the first Tibetan settlement established in Karnataka.
Namdroling Monastery (Golden Temple), founded in 1963 by Penor Rinpoche, houses monumental gilded Padmasambhava, Buddha, and Amitayus statues.
Preserves monastic dialectics, thangka painting, and butter-sculpture crafts.
preservationNote: Monastic libraries and artisan workshops actively train younger monks and community craftspeople.
altText: Monastic architecture of Namdroling Golden Temple in Bylakuppe, Mysuru district.

title: Mysore Pak
recognitionOrEra: Royal Wadiyar Palace Kitchen Lineage · Mysuru
summary: Golden, melt-in-the-mouth roasted gram flour, pure ghee, and sugar-syrup confection invented inside the Mysore Palace kitchens.
description: Created by royal chef Kakasura Madappa inside the kitchens of the Mysore Palace under Maharaja Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV, Mysore Pak blends roasted chickpea flour (besan) with boiling sugar syrup and generous pure cow ghee—giving either a traditional porous golden crunch or soft ghee-rich texture.
verifiedFacts: Tradition attributes its invention to royal chef Kakasura Madappa in the early 20th-century Mysore Palace kitchen.
Descendants of the royal chef continue preparing the confection in historic Mysuru sweet shops.
Core ingredients consist strictly of gram flour, cane sugar syrup, and pure clarified butter (ghee).
preservationNote: Recognized globally as an iconic heritage confection of Mysuru and Karnataka.
altText: Golden cubes of traditional ghee Mysore Pak confection.

title: Raichur Fort & Maski Ashokan Edict
recognitionOrEra: 3rd Century BCE Mauryan & 1294 CE Kakatiya Eras
summary: Cyclopean dry-stone fortress built in 1294 CE above the Krishna–Tungabhadra Doab, complemented by Maski's landmark Ashokan rock inscription.
description: Erected in 1294 CE by Kakatiya governor Gore Gangaya Reddivaru as attested by a monumental 12-meter Telugu-Sanskrit stone slab, Raichur Fort guards the strategic Raichur Doab. Elsewhere in the district at Maski, an Ashokan rock edict discovered in 1915 provided the crucial proof linking 'Devanampriya' with Emperor Ashoka.
verifiedFacts: Raichur Fort's inner citadel features massive cyclopean granite blocks fitted without mortar.
Maski Minor Rock Edict (1915 discovery) was the first inscription found explicitly naming 'Ashoka'.
Mudgal Fort in Lingasugur taluk preserves layered Yadava, Bahmani, and Adil Shahi ramparts.
preservationNote: Monuments protected under the Karnataka State Department of Archaeology and ASI.
altText: Stone ramparts and hilltop enclosure of Raichur Fort in Raichur district.

title: Raichur–Manvi Dasa Sahitya Vocal Tradition
summary: Devotional Kannada keertana and suladi tradition carried forward in the Raichur Doab by saint-composers Vijayadasa and Jagannathadasa.
description: Following Purandaradasa and Kanakadasa, the 18th-century Haridasa movement blossomed in Raichur's Manvi and Chikalparvi through Vijayadasa and Jagannathadasa (author of the philosophical classic 'Harikathamritasara'), whose compositions remain integral to both rural bhajana circles and classical Carnatic concerts.
verifiedFacts: Jagannathadasa (1728–1809 CE) was born at Byagawat and lived in Manvi, composing Harikathamritasara.
Traditional bhajana mandalis sing with tamboori, tala (cymbals), and mrudanga along the Tungabhadra valley.
Manuscripts are archived by Dasa Sahitya research centers across Raichur and Mysuru.
preservationNote: Annual Aradhana music gatherings preserve authentic oral melodies and ragas of Haridasa suladis.
altText: Raichur Manvi Dasa Sahitya Devotional Music Lineage

title: Jolada Rotti & Ennegayi Staple
summary: Hand-patted unleavened sorghum flatbread cooked on hot iron griddles and served with stuffed baby brinjal (ennegayi) and spicy peanut chutneys.
description: Spanning Raichur, Vijayapura, Kalaburagi, Bagalkot, and Dharwad, Jolada Rotti is the beloved agrarian staple of northern Karnataka. Made solely from stone-ground jowar (sorghum) flour and hot water—kneaded without gluten and patted thin by hand—it pairs with ennegayi, jhunka, shenga chutney, and fresh curd.
verifiedFacts: Prepared from white or yellow sorghum (jola) flour bound solely with boiling water.
Includes crisp shelf-stable variants known as 'Khadak Rotti' carried by travelers and farmers.
Accompanied by roasted peanut (shenga), flaxseed (agase), and niger seed (gurellu) powders.
preservationNote: Millet revival cooperatives promote heirloom dryland sorghum varieties across North Karnataka.
altText: Traditional North Karnataka Jolada Rotti meal served with ennegayi curry and chutneys.

title: Ramadevara Betta & Janapada Loka Heritage
recognitionOrEra: Granite Hill Shrine & Folk Arts Sanctuary · Ramanagara
summary: Granite monolith range hosting stone-stepped hill temples above the Arkavathi basin, paired with Karnataka's flagship Janapada Loka folk museum.
description: Rising amidst ancient granite boulders, Ramadevara Betta features stone-cut flights of steps leading to an ancestral Pattabhirama shrine and India's first vulture conservation sanctuary. Nearby, Janapada Loka—founded by folklorist H.L. Nage Gowda—preserves over 5,000 rural artifacts, shadow puppets, and folk instruments.
verifiedFacts: Janapada Loka in Ramanagara curates folk masks, puppets, agricultural tools, and an open-air amphitheater.
Ramadevara Betta granite outcrops safeguard critically endangered long-billed vultures alongside historical shrines.
Nearby Magadi and Savandurga preserve historic fortifications of the Kempegowda dynasty.
preservationNote: Janapada Loka organizes Lokotsava workshops uniting elderly rural artists with school students.
altText: Granite outcrops and hill landscape of Ramadevara Betta in Ramanagara district.

title: Ragi Mudde & Bassaru
summary: Steamed finger-millet (ragi) balls dipped in flavorful greens-and-lentil broth (bassaru) or hyacinth bean curry (avarekalu saaru).
description: The nutritional backbone of Old Mysore agrarian households across Ramanagara, Tumakuru, Mandya, Kolar, and Mysuru, Ragi Mudde is crafted by whisking stone-milled finger millet flour in boiling water into velvety spheres, traditionally swallowed in small bites dipped in soppu bassaru, upsaaru, or winter avarekalu saaru.
verifiedFacts: Finger millet (Eleusine coracana) has been cultivated in southern Karnataka since Neolithic times.
Bassaru pairs boiled leafy greens and lentils with a tempered spice paste roasted on stone grinders.
Rich in calcium and dietary fiber, sustaining agrarian communities across southern and central Karnataka.
preservationNote: Native rainfed ragi varieties are promoted through Karnataka's millet heritage initiatives.
altText: Traditional southern Karnataka Ragi Mudde served alongside seasoned Bassaru broth and greens.

sources.title: Traditional Culinary Heritage of Old Mysore

title: Aghoreshwara Temple, Ikkeri & Keladi Rameshwara
summary: Granite sanctuary at Ikkeri blending Vijayanagara mandapa pillars, Hoysala stellate echoes, and heavy-monsoon coastal roof detailing.
description: Built by the Keladi Nayakas after shifting their capital from Keladi to Ikkeri in the 16th century CE, the Aghoreshwara Temple lacks a traditional outer enclosure wall yet stands on a commanding platform faced by a graceful stone Nandi pavilion, alongside the nearby three-shrine Rameshwara complex at Keladi.
verifiedFacts: Commissioned under Keladi Nayaka rulers (notably Sankanna Nayaka and Venkatappa Nayaka) in the 16th century CE.
Keladi Rameshwara Temple preserves distinctive wooden-ceiling-style stone carvings and a Gandabherunda relief.
Protected as a Monument of National Importance by the Archaeological Survey of India.
preservationNote: ASI Bengaluru Circle manages drainage and monsoon moss conservation across both Ikkeri and Keladi.
altText: Granite Nandi pavilion and sanctuary of Aghoreshwara Temple at Ikkeri in Shivamogga district.

title: Rameshwara Temple & Museum, Keladi
recognitionOrEra: 15th–16th Century CE Keladi Nayaka Seat · ASI
summary: Founding temple complex of the Keladi Nayakas preserving Hoysala-Dravida hybrid motifs, a Gandabherunda ceiling slab, and historical manuscripts.
description: Constructed at the original seat of Chaudappa Nayaka (founder of the Keladi Nayaka kingdom around 1499 CE), the Rameshwara Temple houses adjacent shrines of Rameshwara, Veerabhadra, and Parvati, adorned with carved stone pillars and an on-site museum of Keladi copperplates and palm-leaf manuscripts.
verifiedFacts: Features a celebrated stone ceiling medallion depicting the two-headed Gandabherunda bird.
Adjacent Keladi Museum preserves archival palm-leaf manuscripts, coins, and Nayaka-period weaponry.
Remembers Rani Chennamma of Keladi, renowned for sheltered protection of Maratha king Rajaram against Mughal forces.
preservationNote: Conserved jointly by ASI and the Keladi Museum heritage trust.
altText: Stone prakara colonnade inside the historic Rameshwara Temple at Keladi in Shivamogga district.

title: Veeragase Heroic Folk Dance
summary: Vigorous ritual dance performed with unsheathed ceremonial swords, white turbans, rudraksha garlands, and resonant sammel/karade drums.
description: Rooted in Veerashaiva oral lore recounting Daksha Yajna and performed across Malnad, central, and northern Karnataka (especially Shivamogga, Chikmagalur, Haveri, and Mysuru Dasara), Veeragase performers wear striking crimson-and-white attire, brass anklets, and carry a wooden plaque of Veerabhadra while chanting heroic prose ('odabu').
verifiedFacts: Accompanied by traditional percussion instruments including sammel, karade, and shehnai.
Performers recite spirited rhythmic prose narratives (odabu) prior to synchronized sword-and-shield choreography.
Regularly featured in Karnataka state processions including Mysuru Dasara Jambu Savari.
preservationNote: Patronized by Karnataka Janapada Academy through village troupe stipends and festival invitations.
altText: Veeragase folk performer in traditional white turban, red sash, and ceremonial attire.

title: Chittara Folk Wall & Floor Art (Sagara)
recognitionOrEra: Indigenous Deevaru Women's Folk Painting · Malnad
summary: Intricate geometric white-and-ochre murals painted by Malnad Deevaru women using ground rice paste, red earth, and roasted rice charcoal.
description: Traditionally painted on mud walls and thresholds during harvests and weddings by women of the Deevaru community around Sagara and Soraba in Shivamogga district, Chittara weaves symbolic paddy rows, wedding canopies, peacocks, and ladders using a chewed bamboo-reed brush and natural pigments.
verifiedFacts: Natural palette uses red laterite earth (kemmannu), ground rice paste (white), yellow turmeric, and burnt-rice black.
Geometric motifs ('todu') symbolize agrarian abundance and cosmic order in rural Malnad homes.
Documented by crafts councils and rural design collectives in Sagara.
preservationNote: Artisan workshops adapt Chittara motifs onto handmade paper and textiles while keeping wall rituals alive.
altText: Chittara Folk Wall Art of Sagara in Shivamogga

title: Madhugiri Fort (Monolithic Hill Citadel)
summary: Steep rock-cut hill fortification ascending Asia's second-largest monolithic granite dome, fortified with stone gates, granaries, and water tanks.
description: Crowns a monumental granite hill rising nearly 3,930 feet above sea level in Tumakuru district. Originally fortified in the 17th century by local chieftain Raja Hira Gowda and later reinforced by Hyder Ali, Madhugiri Fort protects rock-hewn staircases, domed granaries (Naviludone, Kumbaradone), and ancient temples.
verifiedFacts: Widely cited as the second-largest monolithic rock dome in Asia after nearby Savandurga.
Contains multiple concentric gateways—Antaralada Bagilu, Diddibagilu, and Mysore Gate—hugging sheer granite slopes.
Protected as a Monument of National Importance by the Archaeological Survey of India.
preservationNote: Heritage trekking stewardship and ASI stone conservation protect the precipitous granite stairways.
altText: Steep monolithic granite hill slope and stone fort walls of Madhugiri Fort in Tumakuru district.

title: Kalleshwara & Channakeshava Temples, Aralaguppe
summary: Twin-era temple village preserving a 9th-century Nolamba brick-and-granite shrine with ceiling reliefs beside a 13th-century Hoysala temple.
description: Tucked in Tiptur taluk of Tumakuru district, Aralaguppe showcases two distinct golden ages in one village: the late 9th-century Nolamba-era Kalleshwara Temple—famous for its carved ceiling panel of a dancing Shiva amidst Ashtadikpalas—and the 13th-century Hoysala soapstone Channakeshava Temple.
verifiedFacts: Kalleshwara Temple preserves one of Karnataka's finest 9th-century Nolamba Pallava stone ceiling sculptures.
Channakeshava Temple (c. 1250 CE) displays classic Hoysala stellate carving signed by artist Honnoja.
Protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.
preservationNote: Maintained by ASI Bengaluru Circle with quiet rural visitor access.
altText: Aralaguppe Nolamba and Hoysala Temples in Tumakuru

title: Siddaganga Trividha Dasoha Heritage
summary: Centuries-old monastic tradition centered on 'Trividha Dasoha'—providing free food, shelter, and education to thousands of students regardless of background.
description: Rooted in the 15th-century Siddaganga Matha and expanded enormously during the 20th century under Dr. Shivakumara Swamiji, Trividha Dasoha exemplifies Karnataka's Sharana ethos of selfless community service—hosting an annual agricultural fair alongside residential schooling for over 10,000 children.
verifiedFacts: Embodies the three pillars of Anna (food), Akshara (literacy), and Ashraya (shelter).
Annual Siddaganga Shivaratri Fair showcases rural farm crafts and indigenous livestock.
Continues as one of Karnataka's most respected living civic-spiritual traditions.
preservationNote: Sustained entirely by community agricultural offerings and institutional trusts.
altText: Siddaganga Trividha Dasoha Tradition in Tumakuru

title: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha & Biennial Paryaya
summary: Coastal temple monastery founded by philosopher Madhvacharya, featuring the Kanakana Kindi window and biennial Ashta Matha Paryaya transfer.
description: Founded in the 13th century CE by Dvaita Vedanta philosopher Madhvacharya, Udupi's Sri Krishna Matha preserves coastal laterite-and-timber architecture around the Madhwa Sarovara tank. Every two years in January, the town celebrates Paryaya—a grand civic and nocturnal procession transferring temple stewardship among Udupi's eight monasteries (Ashta Mathas).
verifiedFacts: Paryaya rotates administrative responsibility sequentially across the eight Mathas every two years on January 18.
Houses the Kanakana Kindi viewing window, honoring 16th-century poet-saint Kanakadasa.
Maintains an unbroken tradition of daily community meals (Anna Prasada) for pilgrims.
preservationNote: Ashta Matha trusts preserve centuries-old Sanskrit palm-leaf manuscripts and wooden temple chariots.
altText: Madhwa Sarovara temple tank and coastal tiled courtyard at Udupi Sri Krishna Matha.

title: Udupi Temple & Vegetarian Cuisine
summary: Sattvic coastal culinary school anchored in coconut, tamarind, curry leaves, GI-tagged Mattu Gulla brinjal, crisp dosa, and idli traditions.
description: Nurtured in the temple kitchens of Udupi Sri Krishna Matha and carried across India by Udupi restaurateurs in the 20th century, Udupi cuisine emphasizes seasonal coastal produce—such as the GI-protected Mattu Gulla brinjal—without onion or garlic in temple meals, alongside crisp masala dosa, kadubu, goli baje, and patrode.
verifiedFacts: Temple culinary lineages evolved strict sattvic menus featuring seasonal gourds, jackfruit, and coconut.
Udupi Mattu Gulla brinjal holds Geographical Indication Application No. 199 (registered 2011).
Inspired the widespread establishment of vegetarian Udupi tiffin rooms across South and West India.
preservationNote: Coastal growers in Mattu village preserve heirloom brinjal seeds alongside traditional temple cooking guilds.
altText: Crisp South Indian masala dosa served in the Udupi restaurant culinary tradition.

title: Udupi Cotton Handloom Sarees
summary: Lightweight, breathable coastal cotton sarees woven in high-count yarn on throw-shuttle pit looms suited to humid Western Ghats summers.
description: Woven by handloom cooperatives across Udupi and Karkala taluks since the 19th-century Basel Mission weaving initiatives and earlier coastal guilds, Udupi sarees feature crisp checked or solid pastel bodies with vibrant contrast borders woven in 60s to 80s combed cotton.
verifiedFacts: Protected under Geographical Indication Application No. 103 (registered in 2008).
Produced through coastal weavers' cooperative societies in Udupi, Brahmavar, and Padubidri.
Known for breathable weave structure adapted to coastal monsoon and summer humidity.
preservationNote: Cooperative societies and Karnataka Handloom programs support younger weavers adopting GI Udupi cotton looms.

title: Madhukeshwara Temple, Banavasi
recognitionOrEra: Kadamba, Chalukya & Sonda Nayaka Eras · ASI
summary: Ancient temple complex in Karnataka's first royal capital Banavasi, housing a 5th-century Satavahana-Kadamba record and finely carved stone cot.
description: Located along the Varada River in Sirsi taluk, Banavasi was the capital of Karnataka's earliest indigenous kingdom—the Kadambas (founded c. 345 CE by Mayurasharma)—and celebrated in verse by poet Adikavi Pampa. Its Madhukeshwara Temple preserves early Kadamba stone fabric, Chalukyan reliefs, and an intricately carved stone cot (mancha) gifted by Sonda rulers.
verifiedFacts: Preserves architectural contributions from Kadambas, Western Chalukyas, Hoysalas, and Sonda Nayakas.
Nearby site yielded a 2nd-century CE Chutu/Satavahana Prakrit inscription of Nagashri.
Celebrated annually during the Government of Karnataka's Kadambotsava cultural festival.
preservationNote: Protected as a Monument of National Importance by the Archaeological Survey of India.

title: Gokarna Mahabaleshwar Temple & Maha Shivaratri Ratha
recognitionOrEra: Ancient Coastal Sanctuary · Annual Maha Shivaratri Chariot
summary: Classical granite coastal sanctuary housing the Atmalinga shrine and hosting a historic tall wooden chariot procession during Maha Shivaratri.
description: Nestled along the Arabian Sea in Kumta taluk, Gokarna is celebrated in classical Sanskrit and Kannada literature. Its granite Mahabaleshwar Temple houses the sacred Atmalinga, and during Maha Shivaratri, thousands pull a towering decorated wooden temple chariot down Car Street.
verifiedFacts: Referenced in classical epics and inscriptions from Kadamba, Vijayanagara, and Keladi Nayaka periods.
Features coastal granite Dravidian architecture with the sacred Kotiteertha stepped tank nearby.
Maha Shivaratri Rathotsava is one of coastal Uttara Kannada's largest annual festivals.
preservationNote: Heritage maintenance teams preserve the historic timber temple chariots and Kotiteertha water tank.
altText: Ceremonial wooden temple chariot of Mahabaleshwar Temple in Gokarna, Uttara Kannada district.

title: Murudeshwar Temple & Kanduka Peninsula
summary: Arabian Sea headland shrine in Bhatkal taluk combining ancient coastal Shaiva sanctity with a monumental 237-foot Raja Gopura tower.
description: Surrounded on three sides by the Arabian Sea atop Kanduka Hill, Murudeshwar Temple links regional legends of the Gokarna Atmalinga with dramatic coastal architecture—crowned by a 20-storey Raja Gopura and overlooking Bhatkal's maritime heritage coastline.
verifiedFacts: Situated on Kanduka Hill jutting into the Arabian Sea in Bhatkal taluk, Uttara Kannada.
Raja Gopura rises over 237 feet, welcoming visitors into the Chalukya-Dravida-inspired complex.
Nearby Bhatkal preserves 16th-century Ketapai Narayana and Jattappa Naik Chandranatha temples.
preservationNote: Coastal erosion monitoring and responsible beachfront management safeguard the headland peninsula.
altText: Towering Raja Gopura of Murudeshwar Temple overlooking the Arabian Sea in Uttara Kannada.

title: Hampi Utsav (Vijaya Utsava)
recognitionOrEra: Annual State Heritage Festival · Vijayanagara District
summary: Three-day cultural festival staged amidst Hampi's illuminated granite ruins celebrating classical Carnatic music, folk parades, and stonecraft.
description: Organized annually by the Government of Karnataka amidst the Tungabhadra boulder landscape of Hampi, Hampi Utsav revives the cultural grandeur of the Vijayanagara Empire—hosting classical music, dance, puppetry, jumbo parades, and artisan exhibitions across stages named after imperial landmarks.
verifiedFacts: Celebrates Vijayanagara heritage in honor of Purandaradasa, Vidyaranya, and Krishnadevaraya.
Includes the Shobhayatre folk procession featuring troupes from across Karnataka's 31 districts.
Concert stages are carefully placed outside sensitive monument plinths under ASI clearance.
preservationNote: Acoustic and lighting limits are strictly enforced by ASI and HWHAMA to protect ancient granite monuments.

title: Purandaradasa & Carnatic Music Foundation
summary: Systematization of Carnatic classical pedagogy (Sarali, Janta Varisai, Geethams) composed by 16th-century Haridasa saint Purandaradasa at Hampi.
description: Revered as 'Sangita Pitamaha' (Grandfather of Carnatic Music), 16th-century poet-composer Purandaradasa lived and sang at Hampi's Vittala Temple complex during the Vijayanagara Empire. His Mayaamalavagowla beginner exercises and thousands of Kannada padas shaped the entire pedagogical architecture of modern South Indian classical music.
verifiedFacts: Introduced Mayaamalavagowla as the foundational raga for teaching Carnatic vocal music.
Tradition holds he composed tens of thousands of Kannada devotional lyrics signed 'Purandara Vittala'.
Commemorated annually at the Purandaradasa Mantapa overlooking the Tungabhadra at Hampi.
preservationNote: Music academies across Karnataka and South India teach his foundational compositions daily.

title: Gol Gumbaz (Mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah)
recognitionOrEra: Completed 1656 CE · Adil Shahi Architecture · ASI
summary: Monumental 17th-century basalt mausoleum crowned by an intersecting-pendentive dome and famed acoustic Whispering Gallery.
description: Built between 1626 and 1656 CE as the mausoleum of Sultan Mohammed Adil Shah (r. 1627–1656), Gol Gumbaz stands as a structural triumph of Deccan Indo-Islamic engineering. Eight intersecting arches support a massive unsupported circular brick-and-mortar dome spanning 44 meters externally, cradling an indoor Whispering Gallery.
verifiedFacts: Outer diameter of the dome measures roughly 44 meters, supported by a clever eight-intersecting-arch pendentive system.
Acoustic Whispering Gallery carries even faint sounds and echoes them multiple times across the rotunda.
Adjacent Naqqar Khana houses the ASI Archaeological Museum of Vijayapura.
preservationNote: Conserved by the Archaeological Survey of India with strict visitor capacity monitoring inside the Whispering Gallery.
altText: Monumental dome, octagonal corner towers, and lawns of Gol Gumbaz in Vijayapura.

title: Ibrahim Rauza Tomb & Mosque Complex
recognitionOrEra: Completed 1626 CE · Adil Shahi Period · ASI
summary: Symmetrical dark-basalt tomb and mosque facing across an ornamental pond on a raised stone terrace, famed for carved Arabic calligraphy and hanging stone chains.
description: Commissioned by Ibrahim Adil Shah II and completed in 1626 CE by architect Malik Sandal, Ibrahim Rauza pairs a finely proportioned tomb and matching mosque atop a raised plinth. Celebrated for delicate pierced stone lattice windows, carved stone chains, and calligraphic cornices, it is widely regarded as the most ornate monument of Bijapur.
verifiedFacts: Designed by Malik Sandal during the reign of Ibrahim Adil Shah II (patron of music treatise Kitab-i-Nauras).
Tomb interior features an unusual flat hanging-slab stone ceiling carved without central pillars.
Protected as a Monument of National Importance by the Archaeological Survey of India.
preservationNote: ASI conserves the carved basalt filigree screens and garden water channels.
altText: Symmetrical domes, slender minarets, and carved basalt arcade of Ibrahim Rauza in Vijayapura.

title: Kudala Sangama Confluence & Basava Jayanti
summary: Sacred river confluence where 12th-century philosopher-reformer Basavanna studied and attained aikya (union), uniting Chalukyan temple heritage with Vachana ideals.
description: Situated at the confluence of the Krishna and Malaprabha rivers in southern Vijayapura/Bagalkot borderland (officially in Hungund/Basavana Bagewadi circuit; Kudala Sangama lies adjacent to Basavana Bagewadi, birthplace of Basavanna), this heritage precinct honors Basavanna's childhood at Basavana Bagewadi and his final resting place at Sangama.
verifiedFacts: Basavana Bagewadi in Vijayapura district is honored as the birthplace of 12th-century reformer Basavanna.
Basava Jayanti commemorates social equality, vernacular Kannada literacy, and Kayaka-Dasoha ethics.
Preserves medieval Chalukyan stone temple architecture and community auditoriums.
preservationNote: Kudala Sangama Development Board and Vijayapura trusts maintain riverfront steps and Vachana archives.

title: Yadgir Hilltop Fort & Surpur Heritage
recognitionOrEra: Yadava, Bahmani & Adil Shahi Eras · State Protected
summary: Granite monolith citadel guarding the Bhima River valley alongside Surpur Bedar Nayaka heritage and Shahpur's natural rock hills.
description: Rising nearly 100 meters above Yadgir town on a massive granite ridge, Yadgir Fort preserves fortified stone gateways, ancient water tanks, cannons, and mosques spanning Yadava, Bahmani, and Adil Shahi rule. Nearby Shorapur (Surpur) preserves Bedar Nayaka heritage and Taylor's Manzil.
verifiedFacts: Inscriptions inside Yadgir Fort confirm fortifications spanning Yadava of Devagiri and 14th–16th century Sultanate phases.
Surpur Fort and Taylor's Manzil honor Raja Venkatappa Nayaka's 1857 resistance and Col. Meadows Taylor's chronicles.
Shahpur hills feature a natural granite formation widely known locally as the 'Sleeping Buddha'.
preservationNote: State archaeology teams document fort inscriptions while local authorities improve heritage access trails.
altText: Historic hilltop view from Yadgir Fort overlooking Yadgir town in the Bhima valley.

title: Surpur (Shorapur) Traditional Garu Painting
recognitionOrEra: 18th–19th Century Bedar Nayaka Court School · Yadgir
summary: Rare Deccan miniature and gold-embossed scroll painting lineage developed under the Bedar Nayaka court of Surpur (Shorapur).
description: Flourishing in the 18th and 19th centuries under the patronage of the Surpur Bedar Nayakas of Yadgir district, Surpur painting combines Deccan and Vijayanagara stylistic idioms with distinctive raised white-paste ('garu') gesso reliefs gilded with gold and natural mineral pigments on cloth and paper.
verifiedFacts: Closely parallels Mysuru and Tanjore gesso schools while preserving distinct Surpur royal portraiture.
Surviving manuscripts and royal portraits from Surpur are housed in museum collections including Salar Jung and Karnataka archives.
Traditional Chitragara descendants in Shorapur work to revive natural pigment techniques.
preservationNote: Documented by Karnataka Lalithakala Academy as a vital northern Deccan court painting heritage.

title: Mailapur Mallayya Makara Sankranthi Jatra
summary: Historic mid-January rural pilgrimage in Yadgir taluk gathering farming and shepherd communities with folk ballads and traditional cattle displays.
description: Every Makara Sankranthi, Mailapur hill in Yadgir district hosts the Sri Mallikarjuna (Mallayya) Jatra—drawing tens of thousands of devotees from Yadgir, Kalaburagi, and neighboring Telangana with traditional folk percussion, blanket offerings, and rural market fairs.
verifiedFacts: Celebrated annually around Makara Sankranthi (mid-January) at Mailapur in Yadgir district.
Strong cultural link with North Karnataka's Kuruba shepherd heritage and Chaudaki folk ballads.
Features traditional blanket (kambali) weaving displays and rural hospitality.
preservationNote: Local panchayats and district administrators coordinate sanitation and water facilities during the annual fair.
